newsitem.title: UK: Airlines face cargo threat from intergrators-Heavy.
newsitem.headline: Airlines face cargo threat from intergrators-Heavy.

text.p: Major scheduled airlines face a growing threat from integrators that will force them to take a closer look at their freighter operations, said HeavyLift Cargo Airlines managing director Michael Hayles.

One way major airlines may move to safeguard their market share is to forge links with specialised cargo carriers like HeavyLift who already works regularly with top airlines including British Airways and KLM.

Such "outsourcing of non-core activities will be one of the lasting features of aircargo in the 1990s," Hayles told SMi's Competitiveness and Profitability in Air Cargo Conference here in a keynote address.
The outsize market is the mainstay of HeavyLift's business but Hayles said it continues to diversify.

In future it be involved in further partnerships with large scheduled carriers who want to offer freight services without owning freighters but who do recognise the advantages of outsourcing to somebody with all-cargo expertise.
Hayles said HeavyLift is committed to acquiring new generation freighter aircraft to operate on behalf of major airlines and is now in advanced discussions with a number of airlines.
Already integrators are moving on from the small parcels market to erode the mid-weight range where airlines and forwarders earn their highest yields.

"On key market sectors scheduled belly-hold space on passenger aircraft is already unable to cope with customer demand," said Hayles adding that "buying their own freighter fleet is a risk few (airlines) are willing - or able - to undertake but the flexibility and control that they can achieve through a good third party partnership can provide a solution."

Hayles said HeavyLift would like to be able to offer solutions ranging from the operation of a single cargo aircraft for an airline through to management of their entire freighter programme. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
